claim_boundary: Both runs are laptop-scale LR/stability diagnostic runs, NOT capability runs. Neither produced a usable checkpoint (36M was superseded by the 171M pilot; 171M was manually interrupted mid-divergence). This is infrastructure + negative-training-dynamics evidence only.

36M_preflight.hardware: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Laptop GPU (sm_120, 8.0 GB VRAM), Windows 11, Python 3.14.6, torch cu128
36M_preflight.architecture: 6L x 384h, GQA 6q/3kv, MoE 8x2 at layers [2,5], 1 Liquid mixer at layer 3, seq 512, global batch 32, max_steps 1830
36M_preflight.optimizer: AdamW8bit (use_galore=True, use_8bit_adam=True, galore_available=False -> GaLore fell back to plain AdamW8bit)
36M_preflight.outcome: DIVERGED, twice, correlated with Liquid unfreeze events

timeline.step_200: Liquid unfreezes (liquid_warmup_steps=200, before LR-warmup-end at 274 and before divergence-guard-arm at 274)
timeline.step_200_270: first explosion: GradNorm 30 -> 2.35e13 (step 230 peak), loss climbs to 30.33 (step 270)
timeline.step_220_liquid_spike_guard: Liquid EMA-relative spike guard trips ('loss>15.06, 3 strikes'), freezes Liquid until step 414 -- this safety mechanism worked as designed
timeline.step_270_320: partial recovery: loss returns to ~10.3, GradNorm drops to ~10K
timeline.step_420_500: second explosion: loss climbs to 19.93 (step 500), GradNorm again into the trillions
timeline.divergence_guard_armed_at: step 274, reference loss_ema=19.7880 (already elevated by the first explosion's tail -- the guard's own reference was contaminated at arm-time)

36M_preflight.root_cause_assessment: liquid_warmup_steps=200 (an ad-hoc value in preflight_run.py, distinct from the pilot yaml's carefully-derived 667) unfreezes Liquid BEFORE the LR warmup completes (274) and before the divergence guard arms (also 274) -- a real ordering bug specific to this script. The pilot yaml's own comment already documented not copying this ad-hoc value.

171M_pilot.hardware: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Laptop GPU (sm_120, 8.0 GB VRAM), Windows 11, Python 3.14.6, torch cu128
171M_pilot.param_count_delta_explanation: This run used an offline test tokenizer (hf-internal-testing/llama-tokenizer, vocab=32000) instead of the canonical 128256-vocab tokenizer, purely for offline/no-auth compatibility. The overlay-verified transformer body (9L, 512h, GQA 8q/2kv, MoE 8x2 at [2,5,8], Liquid at [1,4,7]) matches the canonical pilot spec exactly -- the embedding-table-driven param delta (172,668,035 - 123,380,000 = 49,288,035, closely matching (128256-32000)*512=49,283,072) does not affect the LR/stability question this pilot is designed to answer.
171M_pilot.outcome: DIVERGED, once, NOT correlated with Liquid (Liquid never unfroze -- run stopped before step 667)

timeline.step_10_370: healthy: loss 10.58 -> 9.99, GradNorm 0.5-134926 (climbing but loss still descending), MoE Overflow low
timeline.step_400_560: sustained explosion: GradNorm 2.09e9 (step 400) -> 1.31e12 (step 560); loss peaks at 14.30 (step 540)
timeline.step_450_divergence_guard_armed: reference loss_ema=11.9316 (already slightly elevated above the true ~10.5 baseline by the early-onset instability)
timeline.divergence_guard_never_tripped: loss never exceeded 1.5x the (already-elevated) 11.9316 reference (would need >17.9); the guard is loss-only and does not track grad_norm, so it stayed silent through the entire GradNorm-into-the-trillions episode
timeline.checkpoint_saved: pilot171m_stabilization_step_563.pt (graceful interrupt-save; NOT committed to the repo, per the repo's own checkpoint-retention policy for small validation runs -- see evidence/2026-07-02-laptop-preflight/README.md precedent)

171M_pilot.root_cause_assessment: Liquid-unfreeze-timing does NOT explain this run (Liquid never activated). Divergence onset correlates instead with LR crossing roughly 2.0e-4-2.5e-4 during warmup, in lockstep with MoE Overflow/Balance(std) degrading (0.03->0.15-0.19 across the explosion window). The z-loss effective weight (2e-6, confirmed in this run's own config) is the leading candidate root cause: z-loss's sole purpose is bounding router-logit growth, and its ~50x-under-strength value is consistent with the observed MoE routing instability driving the gradient explosion.

cross_run_finding: Two divergences at two different scales, two different proximate triggers (Liquid-unfreeze-timing vs mid-warmup LR level), both showing the same signature: GradNorm explosion correlated with MoE routing degradation, loss partially protected by clip=2.0, divergence guard (loss-only) never tripping despite catastrophic GradNorm. This points at a shared underlying cause (MoE router regularization, i.e. z-loss) rather than two unrelated bugs.
actions_taken: z_loss_coef changed 1e-4 -> 0.05 in config/config.py (compensates the existing double-multiply so the effective weight lands at 1e-3, the Switch-Transformer/ST-MoE convention) -- CANDIDATE, not verified on real hardware
divergence guard's loss-only blind spot documented in BACKLOG.md/_TR as a new, unfixed finding
no further preflight/pilot re-run planned before the real 45K launch, per explicit user decision
